findings.claim: Practice question 5 is typed '4 marks — Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: 'Required practical' is AQA/Edexcel vocabulary. OCR Twenty First Century Science uses Practical Activity Groups; the pondweed investigation is PAG5 (B3.1.4b).
findings.evidence: spec B3.1.4b 'describe practical investigations into the effect of environmental factors on the rate of photosynthesis PAG5'; PAG table 'PAG5 Photosynthesis'

findings.claim: Practice question 2 (effect of raised CO2 on tomato growth) is flagged '(HT)'.
findings.truth: B3.1.4a is not bold in the tier-authority file, so it is assessed in both Foundation and Higher papers. The flag wrongly tells Foundation students to skip it.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/biology-b-21c-J257-bold.md B3.1: only outcomes 5 and 6 are bold

findings.claim: 'Light intensity decreases with the square of the distance from the source: double the distance, quarter the intensity.' sits in an unflagged collapsible.
findings.truth: The inverse square law is B3.1.5, which is bold and therefore Higher tier only. The rest of that paragraph is B3.1.4a and is both-tier, so a higher-only wrapper round the paragraph would hide both-tier content. An inline '(Higher tier)' tag is the correct flag here.
findings.evidence: bold file B3.1: '**5.** **use the inverse square law to explain changes in the rate of photosynthesis with distance from a light source**'

findings.claim: KC 2 stem: 'The rate of photosynthesis stops increasing when more CO2 is added but not when the temperature is raised.' Keyed answer: carbon dioxide concentration.
findings.truth: If the rate does not rise when CO2 is added, CO2 was not the limiting factor. The stem as written rules out its own answer key. The intended stem is that the rate DOES increase when CO2 is added.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction; spec B3.1.6 on limiting factors

findings.claim: Several question type labels do not match the question asked: L1 Q4 (suggest/explain a mineral deficiency) and L3 Q6 (explain a mutualism) are both labelled 'Compare or Contrast'; L4 Q1 ('Explain why...') is labelled 'Define / Identify'.
findings.truth: Mislabelled command words, not wrong science. This belongs to the question-type relabel queue rather than a content fix.
findings.evidence: internal mismatch between question text and type label

findings.claim: The transpiration glossary entry adds 'driven by the evaporation-cohesion-tension mechanism'.
findings.truth: Not wrong, but the spec states learners are not expected to describe transpiration in terms of tension or pressure, and the in-lesson dfn for the same term omits it.
findings.evidence: spec B3.2 advisory note: 'Learners are not expected to describe transpiration in terms of tension or pressure'

findings.claim: 'The living (biological) part is called the community; the non-living part is called the habitat.'
findings.truth: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. The non-living part of an ecosystem is the abiotic environment (abiotic factors). A student who writes the lesson's definition in an exam loses the mark.
findings.evidence: spec B3.4.1 'explain how some abiotic and biotic factors affect communities'; B3 KS1-3 statement on populations and communities; settled definition

findings.claim: 'In UK grasslands, for example, red and grey squirrels compete for hazelnuts...'
findings.truth: Both squirrel species are woodland animals; grey squirrels displaced red squirrels from broadleaf woodland, not grassland.
findings.evidence: settled fact; Wikipedia (Eastern grey squirrel) confirms spread through England, Wales and southern Scotland and the squirrelpox mechanism

findings.claim: Flashcards 9 and 10 ask 'What does Define mutualism state?' and 'What does Define parasitism state?'
findings.truth: Drafting artefact: the instruction 'Define mutualism' was pasted into a question template. The questions are not readable English.
findings.evidence: internal; garbled text

findings.claim: The lesson gives roughly half its body, 7 of 12 flashcards and 7 practice marks to ecological niche, the competitive exclusion principle, carrying capacity, symbiosis, mutualism, parasitism and trophic cascades.
findings.truth: None of these terms appears anywhere in J257 (greps for 'niche', 'carrying capacity', 'mutualis', 'parasitis' return nothing). B3.3.5 asks only for the importance of interdependence and competition, and B3.4.1 for abiotic and biotic factors. Options: (a) keep the material as enrichment but cut the practice marks and flashcards attached to it; (b) replace roughly half of it with the separate-science-only outcomes B3.3.6-8 (trophic levels, pyramids of biomass, efficiency of biomass transfer) which this unit currently does not teach at all. Recommend (b). Not edited: it would rewrite several narration blocks.
findings.evidence: spec B3.3.5, B3.4.1; terms absent from J257

findings.claim: 'When excess nitrate is washed out of soil by rain, it enters waterways. This process — called eutrophication — triggers algal blooms...'
findings.truth: The name is attached to leaching. Eutrophication is the nutrient enrichment of the water body and the algal bloom, oxygen depletion and die-off that follow. The lesson's own dfn text is correct, so the prose contradicts it.
findings.evidence: spec B3.4 narrative: 'some can cause eutrophication'; internal contradiction with the lesson's dfn

findings.claim: The exam tip says 'Questions on the nitrogen cycle often test the names and roles of specific bacteria', and the key-fact revision tip calls this 'a common exam question'.
findings.truth: J257 names only carbon and water as cycles (B3.3.9, B3.3.10) plus the role of microorganisms in cycling (B3.3.11). 'Nitrogen cycle', 'nitrifying' and 'denitrifying' appear nowhere in the spec, so the exam claim is not supported for this board.
findings.evidence: spec B3.3.9 'including carbon and water', B3.3.10, B3.3.11; grep for 'nitrif' in J257 returns nothing

findings.claim: Takeaway 2: 'The nitrogen cycle depends on four types of bacteria: nitrogen-fixing, nitrifying, denitrifying, and decomposing.'
findings.truth: Decomposers are bacteria AND fungi, as the same lesson states in its own decomposition paragraph. There are three named bacteria types plus the decomposers.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's dfn for decomposers ('mainly bacteria and fungi')

findings.claim: Practice question 2 (fossil fuels vs wood) is flagged '(HT)'.
findings.truth: The carbon cycle is B3.3.10, not bold, so it is assessed at both tiers.
findings.evidence: bold file B3.3: no outcome is bold

findings.claim: Practice question 6 mark scheme ends '(Award 1 mark for both dates correct.)'
findings.truth: 'Award N marks for' is a banned board rubric phrase. The house validator rejects the whole unit while it is present.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_SCIENCE.md banned-string list

findings.claim: Practice question 6 is typed '1 mark — Multiple Choice' but the question gives no options.
findings.truth: It is a two-part recall question. The label tells the student to expect options that are not there.
findings.evidence: internal; no options in the question text

findings.claim: Practice question 4 (geographic isolation and speciation) is flagged '(HT)'.
findings.truth: B6.1.5 covers new species arising through natural selection and is not bold, so it is assessed at both tiers.
findings.evidence: bold file B6.1: no assessable outcome is bold

findings.claim: 'This is why doctors advise completing a full course of antibiotics: stopping early leaves some susceptible bacteria alive, which then recover and multiply.'
findings.truth: The logic is inverted inside a natural-selection explanation. Susceptible bacteria surviving would not select for resistance. It is the least affected cells, the ones most likely to carry resistance, that survive an incomplete course.
findings.evidence: spec B6.1.9 'describe modern examples of evidence for evolution including antibiotic resistance in bacteria'; internal logic

findings.claim: 'modern humans are Homo sapiens and the domestic dog is Canis lupus familiaris' is given as an example of the two-part binomial system.
findings.truth: Canis lupus familiaris is a three-part subspecies name, so it contradicts the sentence it is meant to illustrate.
findings.evidence: settled fact; internal contradiction with the binomial definition in the same paragraph

findings.claim: 'roughly three-quarters of flowering plant species depend on animal pollinators to reproduce'
findings.truth: About 87.5% of flowering plant species are animal-pollinated (Ollerton, Winfree and Tarrant, 2011). The three-quarters figure applies to leading food crop types, not to flowering plant species.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia (Pollinator decline), citing Ollerton et al. 2011: 87.5% of flowering plant species animal-pollinated

findings.claim: 'Biodiversity is the variety of species found in a given area', repeated in the glossary, flashcard 1 and practice question 1 option B.
findings.truth: J257 defines biodiversity in B6.4 as the combination of the diversity of living organisms, the diversity of their genes, and the diversity of ecosystems. The species-only wording is another board's definition and would lose marks on a question asking what biodiversity includes.
findings.evidence: spec B6.4 narrative: 'the combination of the diversity of living organisms, the diversity of genes these organisms have, and the diversity of ecosystems'

findings.claim: 'when sea temperatures rise above a threshold, coral reefs expel the algae they depend on, turning white and dying.'
findings.truth: It is the coral polyps, not the reef, that expel the algae, and bleached coral can recover if the stress ends. The lesson's own knowledge check and dfn stop at 'turning white'.
findings.evidence: settled fact; internal inconsistency with KC 4

findings.claim: The unit slug says 'life on earth / ecosystems'.
findings.truth: Mapping established from the spec: the unit covers Chapter B3 'Living together - food and ecosystems' (L1 photosynthesis and limiting factors = B3.1; L2 = B3.3/B3.4; L3 = B3.3.9-11) and Chapter B6 'Life on Earth - past, present and future' (L4 = B6.1; L5 = B6.3 and B6.4). Board anchors confirmed on this spec: two papers per tier, Breadth (01 Foundation / 03 Higher) and Depth (02 / 04), each 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50%; both papers assess all chapters 1 to 8; the Depth papers carry the 6-mark extended responses; practicals are PAG1 to PAG8. No lesson makes a wrong paper claim.
findings.evidence: spec section 2 chapter list; assessment overview 'Breadth in biology (Components 01 and 03)... 90 marks... content from across all teaching chapters 1 to 8'; section 3j on extended response

findings.claim: Chapter B3 outcomes taught nowhere in this unit.
findings.truth: Missing: B3.1.3a/b enzyme action, lock and key, active site, substrate concentration / temperature / pH, PAG4; the whole of B3.2 except a passing mention of transpiration and root-hair active transport (diffusion, osmosis, active transport and PAG8; partially permeable membranes; xylem and phloem structure and PAG1; translocation; the potometer and PAG6; percentage gain and loss of mass); B3.3.1b qualitative tests for biological molecules, PAG2; B3.3.6, B3.3.7 and B3.3.8 trophic levels, pyramids of biomass and efficiency of biomass transfer, all SEPARATE SCIENCE ONLY; B3.3.12 percentage-of-mass calculations; B3.3.13 and B3.3.14 decomposition rate in aerobic and anaerobic environments and decay-rate calculations, both SEPARATE SCIENCE ONLY; B3.4.2 and B3.4.3 field investigation with quadrats, transects, capture-mark-recapture and indicator species, PAG3, plus means and percentages; bioaccumulation in B3.4.1. Checked against the two fetched sibling units (you-and-your-genes, keeping-healthy): none of this appears there. Caveat: separate-sciences-ocr-b/biology-human-body is still queued and not fetched, so B5.1 may carry diffusion and osmosis for animals; it will not carry plant transport or ecology fieldwork. Recommend a worklist rather than an edit here.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1.3, B3.2.1-8, B3.3.1b, B3.3.6-8, B3.3.12-14, B3.4.1-3; greps of the fetched sibling raw files for osmosis, xylem, phloem, active transport, lock and key, active site, quadrat, pyramid of biomass all return nothing

findings.claim: Chapter B6 outcomes taught nowhere in this unit.
findings.truth: Missing: B6.1.6 impact of selective breeding of food plants and domesticated animals (both tiers; grep for 'selective breeding' across all three fetched units returns nothing, and Darwin's route into natural selection through selective breeding is therefore absent); B6.2.1 advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction, SEPARATE SCIENCE ONLY; B6.4.3 biological factors affecting food security, SEPARATE SCIENCE ONLY; B6.4.2 evaluate evidence for the impact of environmental changes on the distribution of organisms with reference to water and atmospheric gases, which is HIGHER TIER AND SEPARATE SCIENCE ONLY and is the only bold outcome in the whole of B6. B6.4.6 genetic modification is covered in the sibling unit you-and-your-genes L4. Consequence: this unit carries no Higher-tier flagged B6 content at all. Recommend a worklist rather than an edit here.
findings.evidence: spec B6.1.6, B6.2.1, B6.4.2, B6.4.3, B6.4.6; bold file B6.4 shows outcome 2 in bold; grep of fetched sibling raw files

summary: Five lessons checked against OCR Biology B J257 (separate science). Two HIGH content errors: L2 defines a habitat as the non-living part of an ecosystem, and L1's limiting-factor knowledge check states the opposite of what its own answer key needs. One HIGH validator blocker: an 'Award 1 mark for' rubric phrase in L4. The tier fault runs both ways - three practice questions carry a stray '(HT)' on both-tier outcomes, while L1 teaches the inverse square law (B3.1.5, bold) with no flag at all. Three ADJUDICATE items: L2 spends about half its content on niche, competitive exclusion and symbiosis, none of which appears in J257, and large parts of B3 and B6 - including six separate-science-only outcomes - are taught nowhere in the unit or its fetched siblings.
